theme: 3 terms on view controller timing: after it is visible, before it leaves, and after layout

terms.definition: A method that runs after the screen is fully visible.
terms.example: Start the timer in viewDidAppear, so it begins when the user can see the screen.

terms.definition: A method that runs just before the screen goes away.
terms.example: Stop the timer in viewWillDisappear, so it does not run on a hidden screen.

terms.definition: A method that runs after the view has set the size and position of its subviews.
terms.example: Set the gradient frame in viewDidLayoutSubviews, because the final size is known there.

quizzes.question: In this code, which method should hold this line so it runs just before the screen goes away?
quizzes.code:
// stop when the user leaves
stopTimer()

quizzes.question: Which method runs after the view has set the size and position of its subviews?

video.title: viewDidAppear, viewWillDisappear & viewDidLayoutSubviews | Day 118
video.description:
Learn to explain when UIKit calls the view controller lifecycle methods: viewDidAppear, viewWillDisappear & viewDidLayoutSubviews, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
viewDidAppear - A method that runs after the screen is fully visible.
viewWillDisappear - A method that runs just before the screen goes away.
viewDidLayoutSubviews - A method that runs after the view has set the size and position of its subviews.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.description:
Explain viewDidAppear, viewWillDisappear & viewDidLayoutSubviews in iOS by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
viewDidAppear, viewWillDisappear, viewDidLayoutSubviews 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

viewDidAppear - A method that runs after the screen is fully visible.
한국어: viewDidAppear: 화면이 완전히 보인 뒤에 실행되는 메서드

viewWillDisappear - A method that runs just before the screen goes away.
한국어: viewWillDisappear: 화면이 사라지기 직전에 실행되는 메서드

viewDidLayoutSubviews - A method that runs after the view has set the size and position of its subviews.
한국어: viewDidLayoutSubviews: 뷰가 하위 뷰의 크기와 위치를 정한 뒤 실행되는 메서드

In this video, Mina and Jake move a timer and a gradient frame to the right lifecycle methods, in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.

landscape.hook: Can you explain viewDidAppear, viewWillDisappear and viewDidLayoutSubviews in English?

dialogue.title: The timer starts too early

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, the timer starts too early. The screen is not visible yet.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Move it to viewDidAppear, like in the code. It runs after the screen is fully visible.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And I stop it in viewWillDisappear, right?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. viewWillDisappear runs just before the screen goes away.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. Now the gradient frame is wrong.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Set it in viewDidLayoutSubviews. The final size is known there.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Too late. The user would see the wrong frame first.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Does viewDidLayoutSubviews run again after rotation?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, every time the layout changes. So keep it light.
